title: NSIC Rc 560 (Cordillera 1) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 560 is an inbred rice for cool, elevated areas: about 143 days and 4 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 560 is an inbred rice variety for cool, elevated areas, known locally as Cordillera 1. The NSIC approved it in 2019. PhilRice bred it. It matures in about 143 days and averages 4 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 6.6 tonnes in trials.

heroImage.alt: Rice terraces in the cool highlands, where NSIC Rc 560 is meant to grow

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 560, or Rc 560, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 4 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 80 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 6.6 tonnes.
**Watch out for:** bacterial leaf blight, tungro, sheath blight.
**Cooked rice:** low amylose, so soft and tender.

blocks.caption: From PhilRice's catalogue of released varieties (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 560 yield?

On average it gives 4 tonnes per hectare. That is about 80 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 10 cool, elevated areas inbreds in PhilRice's list, which is 3.8 tonnes. But the top yield, 6.6 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 143 days from sowing to harvest. IRRI groups varieties of 100 to 120 days as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as long duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, as PalayCheck advises. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in PhilRice's tests: R resistant, MR moderately resistant, I intermediate, MS moderately susceptible, S susceptible. Some carry a second rating in brackets, as PhilRice lists them.
rows: Took a middling share of damage

blocks.text: So scout early for [bacterial leaf blight](/diseases/bacterial-leaf-blight), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.caption: Grain quality in PhilRice's seed database

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits cool, elevated places such as the rice terraces of the Cordillera, where the nights stay cold. So use it where lowland varieties grow too slowly or set too few grains. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 560?
items.a: It is known as Cordillera 1. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 560 take to harvest?
items.a: About 143 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 560?
items.a: PhilRice lists 4 tonnes per hectare on average, about 80 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 6.6 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start, as PalayCheck advises.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against bacterial leaf blight, tungro, sheath blight. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has low amylose, 17.8 percent. So it cooks soft.
